output.name: Vault check-in times out for remote/VPN users without remote site cache
output.summary: Engineers working from home over VPN see the Vault client hang and check-ins of parts, drawings and large assemblies time out until support configures a remote site cache on their client.

root_cause.text: Likely, remote/VPN Vault clients are not provisioned with a remote site cache by default, so check-ins transfer files directly across the VPN to the central vault and exceed the timeout, especially for large assemblies.

quotes.quote: Checking in a 3,000 part assembly from home fails after 20 minutes.
Set remote site cache; check-in succeeded.

evidence.text: Every listed ticket was resolved the same way, by setting a remote site cache, after which check-in worked.

quotes.quote: Set remote site cache; check-in succeeded.
Set remote site cache; check-in succeeded.

evidence.text: Failures are tied to VPN/home connections rather than specific files, affecting single parts and drawings as well as assemblies.

quotes.quote: Check-in of mount_502.prt times out on VPN.
Check-in of mount_505.drw times out on VPN.

evidence.text: Large assemblies fail after a long wait, consistent with a transfer timeout over a slow link.

quotes.quote: Checking in a 3,000 part assembly from home fails after 20 minutes.

output.fix: Make remote site cache part of the standard Vault client configuration for all remote/VPN users (pushed via client deployment or login policy) so no user starts checking in over VPN without it, instead of setting it per ticket.
